# Data provenance and use

## M0 dataset decision

**Dataset:** deterministic synthetic binary tabular classification data (to be generated by code in M1). No dataset file is downloaded, bundled or committed. No real-world customers, IDs, faces, medical information, audio, images or other private records are used.

**External dataset license:** not applicable to algorithmically generated M1 examples. Generated fixture output must remain disposable and its seed/implementation/hash recorded. Synthetic datasets do not validate real-world fairness, base rates, or business performance.

## Proposed fields (M1 design, subject to schema tests)

Numeric feature columns, a binary label, a synthetic group key for split-leakage checks, and a synthetic sample identifier. No fields are derived from real identities.

## Dependencies and provenance

Initial runtime: pydantic-settings (MIT) and its transitive pydantic package (MIT). Developer checks: ruff (MIT), mypy (MIT), pytest (MIT), pytest-cov (MIT), pre-commit (MIT), pip-audit (Apache-2.0), and gitleaks (MIT). Upstream license/NOTICE and transitive dependency audits must be reverified against the final locked versions before release. Do not infer a model or dataset license from a library license.

## Data handling

No raw production input retention. Only synthetic smoke data may be generated during tests. No data or weights committed to git. M1 adds content-hash manifests; future data deletion and artifact retention must be documented before deployment.
